definitions.explanation: A large bell, especially those in temples or churches.

examples.japanese: {鐘|かね}の{音|おと}が{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like the sound of bells.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きな{鐘|かね}を{見|み}た。
{寺|てら}の{鐘|かね}の{音|おと}が{聞|き}こえる。
examples.english: I can hear the sound of the temple bell.

examples.japanese: {除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね}は、{大晦日|おおみそか}の{夜|よる}に108{回|かい}{突|つ}かれる。
examples.english: The New Year's Eve bell is struck 108 times on New Year's Eve night.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{教会|きょうかい}の{鐘|かね}が{時|とき}を{告|つ}げる。{町|まち}の{人々|ひとびと}はその{音|おと}で{時間|じかん}を{知|し}る。
examples.english: The old church bell announces the time. The townspeople tell the time by its sound.

notes:
{鐘|かね} refers to large bells, especially temple bells.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {鐘|かね}が{鳴|な}る (the bell rings)
- {鐘|かね}を{突|つ}く/{撞|つ}く (to strike a bell)
- {鐘|かね}の{音|ね} (the sound of the bell)

CULTURAL NOTES:
- {除夜|じょや}の{鐘|かね} (New Year's Eve bell - rung 108 times)
- Temple bells ({梵鐘|ぼんしょう}) are important in Buddhism

HOMOPHONE:
- {金|かね} (money) - different kanji

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {鐘|かね}: large bell (temple, church)
- ベル: bell (small, electric)
- {鈴|すず}: small bell, jingle bell
